<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>The future of doing nothing.</b><br>
  <sub>A ten-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens. On purpose, on schedule, and on the beat.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  A young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones. Every so often, something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back to her feet. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A coconut lands on a hermit crab, and the coconut walks off.<br>
  <sub>A stationary-frame video for YouTube in the spirit of the 10-hour lo-fi streams, and an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i>. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime. 16:9, 1080p, 24 fps. Always daytime.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <b>SCHEDULED.</b> More than 90 activities on four timers, each one starting on the next bar of the music.<br>
  <b>SYNTHESIZED.</b> The theme, the ocean, the gulls, the ship's horn: all made by code. No samples, no recordings.<br>
  <b>MILLENNIUM READY.</b> It is always daytime, so midnight never comes. Very little happens.
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<p align="center">
  <sub>Live preview in the browser, then export a YouTube-ready MP4: frame-exact video encoded in the browser, sound mixed in by the server.<br>
  Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. Working notes in <a href="MUSING.md">MUSING.md</a>, the whole schedule in <a href="activities.toml">activities.toml</a>.</sub>
</p>

<details>
<summary><b>SPEC SHEET</b>: the ISL-01, in numbers</summary>

```text
 IDLECORE SYSTEMS 2000 · ISLAND DIVISION        MODEL ISL-01 "CASTAWAY"
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 RUNTIME ......... 10:00:00 by default, seed 1992. same seed, same schedule
 PICTURE ......... 16:9, 1080p, 24 fps. hard cuts and stepped movement
 TIME OF DAY ..... daytime. always. there is no night setting
 OPERATOR ........ one. brown hair in a loose low bun, cream headphones,
                   coral tank top, cream shorts, bare feet
 FIXTURES ........ one tall palm, one raft, one bar of signal (at the
                   top of the palm)
 SCHEDULE ........ more than 90 activities on four timers. see ORBIT
                   TABLE
 BEAT GRID ....... every activity starts on the next bar. one bar = 3 s
 DUTY CYCLE ...... busy about a third of the time, idling the rest
 SCENE LIFE ...... 26 entries. built: shore waves, drifting cloud
                   shadows. planned: distant birds, planes with vapour
                   trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers,
                   a gecko and a rain shower
 SOUND ........... more than 150 files, every one synthesized from code
 SAMPLES ......... 0
 LISTENED TO ..... not yet, by anyone. this sheet is all we have
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>ORBIT TABLE</b>: the four timers, and what a typical ten hours holds</summary>

```text
 ORBIT        COMES ROUND EVERY   PER 10 H RUN   FOR EXAMPLE
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 regular      2 to 5 minutes      about 155      a coconut sip, fishing,
                                                 jogging laps, a sandcastle
 occasional   12 to 25 minutes    about 30       the bottle, the turtle,
                                                 coconut vs hermit crab
 rare         30 to 60 minutes    about 13       the drone, the cat, the
                                                 shark, the signal hunt
 super rare   3 to 6 hours        about 2        she walks out over the
                                  (at most 3)    water. she comes back
 chained      when another one    about 20       the bottle's reply, the
              says so                            kumara coming into leaf
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 counts: the median of 200 simulated runs, as the schedule's own header
 says. lanes let things overlap, so the sea can be busy while she is.

 the readout in the banner packs six events into 60 seconds. the real
 island manages about one every three minutes, and idles in between.
 the brochure has been sped up for your convenience.
```

Run [`python tools/schedule.py`](tools/schedule.py) to check the schedule and simulate a ten-hour run.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>GAG MODULES G01 TO G08</b>: what is orbiting the logo</summary>

```text
 G01  SEA TURTLE ........ swims in for a visit. they both doze off
 G02  BOTTLE ............ a message, thrown. it washes straight back to
                          her feet. later, a different bottle brings a
                          reply
 G03  DRONE ............. lowers a parcel and leaves. inside: another
                          pair of headphones. a wave takes the empty box
 G04  GREY TABBY ........ white chest. arrives on a crate, climbs the
                          palm, naps, and one day floats away again. it
                          comes back another time
 G05  SHARK ............. surfaces in headphones and nods to the same
                          beat
 G06  COCONUT ........... falls on a hermit crab, then walks off with the
                          crab wearing it
 G07  ONE BAR ........... the signal hunt. there is exactly one bar of
                          signal on this island, at the top of the palm
 G08  ICED COFFEE ....... she could leave any time. she walks out over
                          the water and comes back with an iced coffee

 ALSO IN SERVICE ........ a tour boat of selfie-takers. a bro on an
                          electric hydrofoil who throws a shaka and
                          carves off. fire by friction, a hammock, a
                          lookout up the palm, spear fishing. a kumara,
                          planted, that grows over the video. a
                          sandcastle the tide takes. waving for rescue
 NOT PICTURED ........... a ship. it went past while you were reading
                          this list
```

<details>
<summary><b>SERVICE MANUAL</b>: the tools, the sound and the export</summary>

```text
 python tools/serve.py ............ the renderer: a web page with a live
                                    preview at http://127.0.0.1:8765/
 export ........................... frame-exact H.264 in the browser
                                    (WebCodecs: 68 to 78 frames a second
                                    in Chrome, measured at 1080p30). the
                                    server mixes the sound and joins the
                                    two into an MP4
 python tools/schedule.py ......... validates the schedule, simulates a
                                    ten-hour run
 python tools/render_demo.py --dev  a dev reel of every activity with a
                                    heads-up display (the older Python
                                    reference renderer)
 python tools/make_audio.py ....... synthesizes all of the sound from
                                    code: no samples, loops or
                                    recordings, so no third-party
                                    licence applies
 theme ............................ a seamless 60 s loop. 80 BPM, F
                                    major, ii-V-I-vi, 20 bars of exactly
                                    3 s. electric piano, kalimba lead,
                                    soft drums, vinyl crackle
 ocean ............................ also a seamless 60 s loop
 levels ........................... -14 LUFS, true peak at or below
                                    -1 dBTP. master and per-routine
                                    volume
 status ........................... in development. no video has been
                                    published yet, so there is no link
```

The files: [tools/serve.py](tools/serve.py), [web/index.html](web/index.html), [tools/schedule.py](tools/schedule.py), [tools/render_demo.py](tools/render_demo.py), [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py).

</details>
